confirmed: 目标是开发一款用于清理电脑存储空间的软件。
candidates: 目标平台：Windows、macOS 或跨平台
核心功能：清理临时文件、系统缓存、浏览器历史记录、大文件、重复文件以及卸载残留
界面类型：图形用户界面（GUI）或命令行界面（CLI）
清理模式：一键快速清理、自定义深度扫描或定时自动化清理
assumptions: 软件界面首选语言为中文
软件主要在本地运行，不需要复杂的云端存储或多端同步功能
软件主要面向个人电脑用户（非企业级服务器或大规模集群管理）
unknowns: 具体的支持系统（仅限 Windows，还是需要跨平台支持）？
目标用户群体是谁（普通电脑用户还是开发者等技术人员）？
是否有偏好的开发技术栈（如 Electron, Qt, Python, Rust, Go 等）？
是否需要清理特定类型的文件（例如开发缓存 node_modules、设计临时文件等）？
对于清理深度和安全性的要求是什么（是否需要清理系统级文件，需要管理员权限）？
risks: 误删风险：误删系统关键文件或用户重要数据，导致系统崩溃或数据丢失
安全杀毒软件误报：由于涉及大量文件删除和系统扫描，可能会被 Windows Defender 或其他杀毒软件误报为恶意软件
扫描性能瓶颈：如果磁盘文件极多，扫描可能会占用极高的 CPU 和 I/O 资源，导致电脑卡顿

gaps.dependency: None (this is the foundational technical decision)
gaps.impact: This directly dictates the programming language, framework/tech stack (e.g., Win32 API vs Electron/Qt), system API access patterns, and delivery timeline.
gaps.reason: It is unresolved whether the application should support only Windows or be cross-platform (macOS, Linux).

gaps.impact: Determines user interface complexity (one-click clean vs. customizable scan paths/filters), default safety boundaries, and the degree of transparency needed during scanning/cleaning.
gaps.reason: The target user persona (ordinary PC users vs. developers/technical personnel) is unresolved.

gaps.impact: Determines the complexity of scanning algorithms, risks of file locking, and the extent of user-customizable options in the MVP.
gaps.reason: The types of files to be cleaned (system junk, browser caches, node_modules, design temp files) are unresolved.

gaps.impact: If administrator privileges are required (e.g., to clean system-level logs or installer caches), it increases the risk of system instability, security auditing issues, and antivirus/Windows Defender false positives.
gaps.reason: The cleaning depth and permission requirements (User vs. Administrator) are unresolved.

gaps.impact: Affects scanner performance (I/O and CPU bottlenecks), executable size (crucial for a disk-saving utility), UI responsiveness, and compatibility with the target OS.
gaps.reason: There is no preferred technology stack (Electron, Qt, Python, Rust, Go, etc.) selected.

conflicts: Targeting ordinary PC users (Assumption) potentially conflicts with cleaning specialized files like developer caches/node_modules (Unresolved Cleanup Targets), which are irrelevant and confusing for non-technical users.
The risk of system crash/data loss (Risk) conflicts with the lack of definition regarding safety rules or user permission boundaries (Unresolved Cleanup Depth/Security requirements).

options.impact: Enables deep integration with Windows APIs (like Registry, Volume Shadow Copy, WinSxS) and allows using native, fast UI technologies (like WPF/WinUI or lightweight Rust/C++).
options.label: (Recommended) Windows only (highly integrated, lightweight native app)

options.impact: Requires a cross-platform framework (e.g., Electron, Tauri, or Qt) and restricts deep system-level cleaning to common user-space directories, unless extensive platform-specific code is written for each OS.
options.label: Cross-platform (Windows, macOS, Linux)

questions.question: Which operating systems should the storage cleaning software support?
questions.reason: The choice between a Windows-only tool and a cross-platform tool directly dictates the UI framework (e.g., native Win32/WPF vs. Electron/Tauri), access to low-level system APIs, and development velocity.
questions.recommendation: Windows only (highly integrated, lightweight native app)
questions.recommendation_reason: Since your current environment is Windows and Windows has very specific/complex system storage locations, starting with a Windows-native focus allows us to write a lightweight, highly effective tool with deep integration before worrying about cross-platform abstractions.

options.impact: Zero risk of breaking the OS. No annoying Windows UAC prompts. Easiest to distribute and run safely.
options.label: (Recommended) Standard User permissions (safest, cleans user-space caches and temp files)

options.impact: Allows reclaiming more space (like WinSxS or system logs), but carries high risk of system instability and will trigger Windows User Account Control (UAC) prompts.
options.label: Administrator permissions (deepest, cleans system logs, Windows updates, and driver backups)

questions.question: What level of system permissions and cleaning depth should the software target?
questions.reason: Requiring Administrator privileges enables cleaning system-wide logs, driver backups, and installer caches, but increases the risk of system instability, security warnings, and antivirus false positives.
questions.recommendation: Standard User permissions (safest, cleans user-space caches and temp files)
questions.recommendation_reason: Starting with user-space directories (e.g., user temp folders, browser caches, developer package caches) is safer, prevents accidental OS damage, avoids UAC prompts on startup, and doesn't trigger security/antivirus warnings.

options.impact: The UI will focus on transparency, scan rules, and lists of specific dev caches. Safe defaults are still key, but users get full visibility and control.
options.label: (Recommended) Developers and technical users (custom paths, regex filters, package manager/build cache cleaning)

options.impact: UI will be extremely simple, focusing on a single 'Scan & Clean' button with minimal configuration, hiding technical details behind simple categories (e.g., 'Temporary Files', 'Browser Data').
options.label: Ordinary PC users (one-click scan, simple cleanup categories)

questions.question: Who is the primary target audience for this space-cleaning software?
questions.reason: Ordinary PC users need a simple, foolproof one-click cleaning experience, while developers and technical users need fine-grained control and targeted cleanup of huge developer directories (e.g., node_modules, Docker layers, build caches).
questions.recommendation: Developers and technical users (custom paths, regex filters, package manager/build cache cleaning)
questions.recommendation_reason: Standard PC users are already well-served by built-in tools like Windows Storage Sense. Developers, however, suffer from massive, hidden space hogs (like duplicate node_modules folders) that general-purpose cleaners ignore. Targeting technical users provides a clear, high-value niche.
